dehydrated_text:
Remember before the Roman Empire, remember the problem of the Iliad. In the Iliad, Achilles cannot forgive himself for his actions, even though his prime forgave him. During that time, we all did good and evil. Forgive ourselves as long as we find the power to do so, we will save the world. But by the time of the Romans, they are pure evil—demonic. You don't forgive yourself then. How do you explain the fact that the Romans conquer the world for pure evil while you, a person who did good, remain a slave?

How do you find comfort and source in this contradiction? The message Jesus came to convey is why the Romans triumphed. According to Jesus, the Romans triumph because the world we live in is false—a dead corpse. This isn't the true world; what matters is up there. So, the Romans have won by being evil.

In the grand scheme of things, they've lost. Think about Achilles: he got what he wanted by betraying Petroles and sacrificing Petroas. He can't sleep or eat because he knows his actions were evil. This is just the Roman way. Jesus tells us to use our imagination, heart, and empathy to understand that even the rich and powerful are tormented by demons. They hate themselves and the world around them.

When you see this for yourself, you realize they are more pitiful than you are. You may be poor, but you're not haunted by demons. To do good in the world, forgive your enemy and love them because only by loving your enemy can you release them from their demons, saving the world. The enemies who oppress us, the rich and powerful—they are like Achilles after they've killed Hector, with no purpose in life.

They are haunted by demons, and we have to kiss their hand, submit before them so that they can be released from their demons. This will make the world a better place. That is the message of Jesus: in times of evil, look at your hearts and others', forgive your enemies, let go of hatred, and save the world.

Jesus taught a message of love and forgiveness, which made him popular because it reminded people of who they are. You may be a slave or think you're worthless, but there's still a spark inside that connects you to the monad. Use love, forgiveness, compassion, and this spark will activate, freeing you from slavery.

The Romans killed Jesus because he was a rebel trying to subvert the natural order.
